subject: Staggered renewal grace (45d) & termination-for-convenience options — legal redlines
messages:
From: Jessica Hoffman <jessica.hoffman@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on renewal & termination language

Hi Sofia,

Quick question as we're reviewing the MSA and Order Form: Acme's procurement team prefers a 45-day notice window for opt-outs to match our internal billing cycle. We also need clarity on the 'Termination for Convenience' mechanics — specifically whether there are any pro-rated credits or early termination obligations if we end the Order Form mid-quarter.

Can Redwood provide suggested contract language (MSA + Order Form) that: 1) supports a staggered 45-day auto-renew waiver for pilot customers, and 2) outlines a clean, customer-facing termination-for-convenience option with any refund/credit mechanics spelled out?

We're aiming to finalize redlines by EOD Thursday so our legal can circulate. I can loop procurement leads into any follow-ups.

Thanks,
Jessica Hoffman
Sr. Procurement Manager | Acme Corporation
(attachment: none)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Hoffman <jessica.hoffman@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on renewal & termination language

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear ask.

We can support a 45-day staggered grace/notice window for pilot or small accounts; there are a few operational implications I want to flag upfront so legal and procurement are aligned:

- Billing cadence mismatch: If your billing closes monthly, a 45-day opt-out means we may need pro-rated token/usage reporting to reconcile the final invoice.
- Auto-renew toggle: We can add language to the Order Form to allow a one-time auto-renew waiver for the first renewal term for pilots (explicit opt-out must be submitted 45 days prior).
- Termination-for-Convenience (TFC): Redwood typically offers TFC with a 60-day notice and a pro-rated refund of pre-paid fees for unused committed capacity. We can consider 45-day TFC for pilot tiers with a modest early-exit fee to protect reserved capacity.

Karthik — looping you and Lauren to draft defensible redlines (MSA + Order Form) that balance Acme's request and our capacity economics. Can you produce a marked-up MSA + Order Form and a short ops checklist for billing reconciliations?

Jessica — will send an initial redline within 24 hours.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Jessica Hoffman <jessica.hoffman@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on renewal & termination language

Sofia/Jessica — attached are proposed redlines: MSA_Redlined_45d_v1.docx and OrderForm_Redline.pdf. High level summary below.

Key changes (MSA):
- Section 2.1 (Term and Renewal): Added a new subsection allowing a one-time "Pilot Renewal Waiver" where the Parties may agree in the Order Form to a 45-day opt-out notice for the first renewal term. Language includes a clear expiration of the waiver at the start of the subsequent term unless re-negotiated.
- Section 8.4 (Termination for Convenience): Added an optional paragraph for pilot-tier customers that allows TFC with 45 days' notice in exchange for an early-exit charge equal to 15% of the remaining committed fees (pro-rated). Standard enterprise customers retain 60-day default.

Key changes (Order Form):
- New checkbox: "Apply Pilot Renewal Waiver (45-day opt-out)" with toggles for: Pilot Tier / Standard Tier, Early-Exit Fee %, and Billing Reconciliation instructions.
- Billing Reconciliation Addendum: brief ops runbook describing final invoice pro-rating, token-level usage export, and timing for refunds (net 30 after final invoice).

Ops implications (for Sofia/Finance):
- If Acme selects the Pilot Renewal Waiver, finance must enable provisional refunds and a manual reconciliation flow. I included a sample Recon Checklist page in the PDF.

I've preserved the default enterprise positions in the MSA and made the pilot language an opt-in via the Order Form so we don't change global defaults.

Attachments: MSA_Redlined_45d_v1.docx (redline), OrderForm_Redline.pdf (render + ops checklist).

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
(attachment: MSA_Redlined_45d_v1.docx, OrderForm_Redline.pdf)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Jessica Hoffman <jessica.hoffman@acme.com>
Date: 2028-03-23T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on renewal & termination language

Thanks Karthik — looked good at a high level. A couple of edits from legal/finance POV:

1) Narrow the pilot TFC carveout: change early-exit charge from 15% of remaining committed fees to the greater of (a) 10% of remaining committed fees or (b) pro-rated cost of reserved GPU hours (so we can cover infra procurement). This prevents outsized revenue erosion for long-duration reserved pools.

2) Add a cap: early-exit charge cannot exceed three months of average monthly committed fees.

3) Clarify refund timing: refunds for pre-paid fees should be processed net-45 days after final reconciliation (we need an extra two weeks for chargebacks and intercompany billing).

4) Ops checklist: move the manual steps for token export to a separate internal-only annex (Order Form should reference but not include the internal checklist).

Jessica — if Acme is comfortable with the above, we'll incorporate and send a DocuSign-ready redline. We prefer the pilot exemption to be an explicit opt-in on the Order Form (checkbox + signature line) to avoid accidental application.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Jessica Hoffman <jessica.hoffman@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-24T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on renewal & termination language

Appreciate the fast turnaround — the updated redlines look reasonable. Two quick asks before we execute:

1) Can you replace the term "early-exit charge" with "capacity protection fee" in the MSA/Order Form so our legal team can present it internally as a non-punitive reconciliation mechanism?

2) Please include the DocuSign link and the HubSpot record in the email when you send the final redline so procurement can track execution.

If those tweaks are editorial, we're ready to sign once the DocuSign packet is live.

Thanks,
Jessica
Sr. Procurement Manager | Acme Corporation
